# Databricks Workspace Architecture Description

## Catalog & Discovery
Our platform uses Unity Catalog as the central governance layer, accessed via the
Unity Catalog API / catalog API. We rely on a three-level namespace
(catalog.schema.table) across all workloads. Schema introspection is performed via
information_schema and column metadata queries. All data is stored in Delta Lake
(open format), and we make heavy use of Delta time-travel / version history.
A shared metastore enables cross-workspace discovery.

## SQL Access
Analysts query through a serverless SQL Warehouse (SQL endpoint) with a shared metastore.

## Lineage & Provenance
UC lineage is enabled with lineage tracking across the estate. We capture
column-level lineage (fine-grained lineage) and expose it via the lineage API
(programmatic lineage). DLT pipeline lineage / delta live lineage is captured for
all Delta Live Tables pipelines.

## Data Quality
We enforce data quality using DLT expectations (delta live expectations / data quality
rules) on every production pipeline, with schema enforcement active.

## Access Control & Identity
Access is governed with UC permissions (grant/revoke) at the catalog level. Sensitive
columns use dynamic masking (column masking) and row-level security (row filters).
Automated jobs authenticate with a service principal (machine identity), and we enforce
token management with a strict token policy (PAT restrictions).

## Observability & Audit
Audit logging is enabled via system tables (audit log). We capture data access logs
(read/write logs) and use billing tables for cost attribution (spend per workspace).
DLT pipeline observability / pipeline metrics and MLflow experiment tracking
(mlflow logging) are monitored on dashboards.

## Real-Time
Structured streaming powers our real-time ingestion with zero-ETL style pipelines.
We use streaming tables and real-time pipelines, with change data feed (CDC) enabled
and incremental processing (micro-batch). Ingestion uses Auto Loader (cloudFiles).
